en: Now last but not least, before we also
explore some examples,
it's really practice that makes perfect. And
that is true for everything in life, that is
true for everything in coding, and that is
also true for algorithms and for solving
problems.
This course gives you a lot of practice. We
see a lot of examples in this course, a lot
of patterns, a lot of important approaches
when it comes to solving problems.
And that really is the key.
Finding good approaches to solve a problem
takes practice. There is no simple
blueprint. There is no formula which you can
apply to every problem.
Instead, you really need to collect a lot of
patterns, a lot of tricks, a lot of
approaches which you saw in various
algorithms. And with all of that in mind,
you'll be able to solve problems with tricks
you learned from another algorithm maybe.
So it's really that practice that matters.
And therefore you should dive into a lot of
common algorithms, practice with interview
questions, and you'll find a ton of
resources regarding that all over the web
outside of that course as well. And I will
share a couple of nice resources on that
later in the course. I can really just
encourage you to use that, to use Google,
and to practice a lot. Because you can take
a 30-hour algorithms course, if you don't
practice on your own, you will not get a
better feeling for coming up with your own
algorithms, you will not really be able to
solve problems. So that is a key part.
